# Delayed HEVC parameter sets: local FFmpeg patch and software regression

**AI disclosure:** This file, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the contributor's request.

Bounded deliverable for [omarchy-m1-video#44](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/44).
Parent [omarchy-m1-video#15](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/15)
stays open: this is a **software-only client candidate**, not a VA-API or hardware
result, and it does not change the HEVC 144/147 count. Nothing here is installed,
packaged or sent upstream.

## Problem

`VPSSPSPPS_A_MainConcept_1` puts all parameter sets before the six pictures, in an
order where each one can precede the parameter set it refers to (for example PPS 3
names SPS 1 thirteen NAL units before SPS 1 appears, and SPS 3 names VPS 1 before
VPS 1 appears). H.265 only requires a referenced parameter set to be available when
the referring one is *activated* by a slice.

FFmpeg n9.0.1 (`libavcodec/hevc/ps.c`) parses a PPS against its SPS, and an SPS
against its VPS, at arrival. When the dependency is missing it logs
`SPS %u does not exist.` / `VPS %d does not exist` and discards the NAL, so slices
later fail with `PPS id out of range`. At the pinned commit the vector decodes to
two pictures (352x288 and 1280x720), MD5 `ec9f5857591ac4c215d194deaf52167c`,
matching the published two-frame failure in `docs/CODEC_STATUS.md`.

The same rule also dropped valid state in two other legal orderings: a PPS sent
before the SPS that *replaces* its SPS id, and an SPS sent before the VPS that
replaces its VPS id. `remove_sps()`/`remove_vps()` deleted the dependants outright.

## Patch

[`ffmpeg-n9.0.1-hevc-pending-parameter-sets.patch`](ffmpeg-n9.0.1-hevc-pending-parameter-sets.patch)
applies to FFmpeg `bf1b838f2ab88b4f8fd83443325c782ea0e0f7fa` (tag `n9.0.1`) and
touches `libavcodec/hevc/ps.c`, `ps.h`, `hevcdec.c`, `hevcdec.h` and `parser.c`.

**Keeping parameter sets.** An SPS or PPS becomes a `HEVCPendingPS` instead of
being discarded when:

* its dependency (the VPS of an SPS, the SPS of a PPS) is absent;
* it fails to parse while its dependency is present, since validity can depend on
  that dependency's content (for example `diff_cu_qp_delta_depth` against the SPS
  coding-block sizes, or `sps_max_sub_layers` against the VPS); or
* the parameter set it was parsed against is replaced (`remove_sps()` and
  `remove_vps()` move dependants to pending instead of freeing them).

At most one entry exists per id, and a newer parameter set with that id (stored,
repeated or pending) supersedes it. Stored state is never deleted by deferral.
For a deferred SPS only its ids are read, without logging. Multi-layer (MV-HEVC)
extension SPSs, whose layout comes from the VPS, are not deferred and fail as
before.

**Sharing, not copying.** Stored `HEVCSPS`/`HEVCPPS` bytes are now RefStruct
buffers with input padding. A pending entry takes a reference to those bytes and
records the exact bit length and start position of the original parse, so
replacing a VPS or SPS costs reference counting, not copies.

**Lazy resolution.** Nothing is parsed again when parameter sets arrive or are
replaced. `ff_hevc_ps_activate()` runs at the first slice of each picture, in the
decoder (`hevcdec.c`, before `hls_slice_header()`) and in the HEVC parser
(`parser.c`). It parses at most the pending SPS and the pending PPS that picture
needs, with `init_get_bits()` over the original bit length, so a late parse reads
exactly what an on-time parse would. An entry that failed is not tried again
until its dependency id refers to a different parameter set (compared by
reference, which the entry holds), so a failing entry costs nothing per picture.

**Activation.** An entry whose dependency has not arrived is the newest parameter
set for its id:

* A pending PPS refuses the picture, since a PPS may change at any picture
  (H.265 7.4.3.3).
* A pending SPS refuses only IRAP pictures, since an SPS with the active id may only
  change at the start of a coded video sequence (7.4.3.2.1); until then the stored
  SPS remains the active one. Pictures that follow a refused IRAP picture are refused
  until the next IRAP picture (`HEVCContext.ps_refused_irap`).
* An entry that failed to parse does not refuse anything: the stored parameter set
  with that id stays usable, as when unpatched FFmpeg rejects a malformed
  replacement.

Frame threads copy the pending lists and `ps_refused_irap` like the stored lists.
Entries are never modified after publication.

**Trade-off for damaged streams.** A repeated PPS whose SPS id is corrupted now
refuses pictures until that PPS id is sent again, where unpatched FFmpeg would keep
decoding with the previous PPS; that is what the spec's replacement semantics
require, and `corrupted-repeat-pps-mid-gop` measures it. A corrupted repeated SPS
in the middle of a GOP has no effect. The HEVC parser has no refused-IRAP state; it
only extracts stream properties.

**Bounds.** Pending state is at most 16 SPS + 64 PPS entries, each referencing
bytes that a stored parameter set or an arriving NAL already held. Replacing a
VPS or SPS moves at most 16 + 64 references. Parsing happens only at activation:
at most one SPS and one PPS per picture, and a failed entry only once per
distinct dependency. Dependencies are typed VPS ← SPS ← PPS, so a cycle cannot be
expressed; the "cyclic" case in #44 is covered by replacement churn and
never-arriving dependencies below.

## Run

On a Linux host with a C toolchain, make, git, Python 3 and an `ffmpeg` with
`libx265` (used only to generate fixtures). The FFmpeg build is software-only and
needs no VA-API, libdrm or other system libraries. No VA device, sudo or
installation.

```sh
# The vector is download-on-demand only; --download fetches it from ITU and checks
# the archive MD5 and the corpus-manifest SHA-256. --vector PATH uses a local copy.
python3 experiments/hevc-parameter-sets/run.py --download

# Also build the patched decoder with ASan/UBSan and repeat every check under it.
python3 experiments/hevc-parameter-sets/run.py --download --sanitize

# Full JCT-VC-HEVC_V1 before/after comparison (Fluster f3ad284, resources downloaded
# with `python3 fluster.py -r RES download JCT-VC-HEVC_V1`), plus every vector
# decoded again with its parameter-set runs reversed.
python3 experiments/hevc-parameter-sets/run.py --download --skip-fixtures \
  --suite-json fluster/test_suites/h.265/JCT-VC-HEVC_V1.json --suite-resources RES \
  --suite-modes auto,single,frame4 --suite-reorder

# Unit tests for the fixture NAL rewriter, the suite gate and the pins
# (no FFmpeg; runs in CI).
python3 experiments/hevc-parameter-sets/tests.py
```

`build-ffmpeg.sh WORK [--sanitize]` fetches exactly the pinned commit, applies the
patch in a separate worktree (reused only while a marker records the same patch
SHA-256) and builds a minimal `ffmpeg` into `WORK` (default
`~/.cache/omarchy-hevc-parameter-sets`); `--sanitize` builds only the patched tree.
`run.py` exits non-zero on any failure and prints a JSON report (`--output FILE`).

Every fixture and vector decode keeps native picture sizes (`-noautoscale`) and is
repeated with FFmpeg's automatic threading, `-threads 1`, and
`-threads 4 -thread_type frame`.

## Checks

**Original vector.** SHA-256 `8501a5e5…` from the driver corpus manifest. The
unpatched build must reproduce the documented failure exactly (exit status 0, two
pictures, MD5 `ec9f5857591ac4c215d194deaf52167c`). The patched build must produce all
six pictures at 176x144, 320x240, 352x288, 640x480, 704x576 and 1280x720 with MD5
`1ddf74263cb4953cfdfcf99c563d88ea`.

**Synthetic fixtures** (generated at run time with libx265 from lavfi test
sources; never committed). The expected output is the *unpatched* decoder's output
for untouched encoder streams (or, for `equivalent`, for the same parameter sets in
on-time order), concatenated at native size, so the oracle does not depend on the
patch. Every fixture kind also states what the unpatched build must do, and the
runner fails if it does not.

| Fixture | Kind | Checks | Unpatched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical-a`, `canonical-crop-c` | unchanged | encoder order, including a conformance (crop) window | pass |
| `truncated-tail-a` | same-as-base | last slice cut in half: identical to unpatched | pass |
| `reversed-order` | delayed | PPS, SPS, VPS order | 0 pictures |
| `remapped-ids-delayed` | delayed | non-zero ids, each referenced before it arrives | 0 pictures |
| `resolution-changes-delayed` | delayed | 176x144 → 640x360 → cropped 350x286, new sets out of order | wrong pictures |
| `pps-before-replacement-sps` | delayed | PPS sent before its replacement SPS | 6 of 12 |
| `sps-before-replacement-vps` | delayed | SPS sent before its replacement VPS | 6 of 12 |
| `pending-across-access-units` | delayed | pending SPS created in one access unit, used in a later one (crosses frame-thread contexts) | wrong pictures |
| `pps-survives-incompatible-intermediate-sps` | delayed | a pending PPS invalid for an intermediate SPS (`diff_cu_qp_delta_depth` 3 vs 16x16 CTBs) decodes with the compatible replacement SPS | 0 pictures |
| `pps-survives-present-incompatible-sps` | delayed | same, with the incompatible SPS present when the PPS arrives | 0 pictures |
| `sps-survives-present-incompatible-vps` | delayed | an SPS with two sub-layers, invalid for a one-sub-layer VPS, decodes with the replacement VPS | 0 pictures |
| `unresolved-replacement-pps-not-stale` | delayed | pictures whose newest PPS waits for its SPS are refused, not decoded with the older PPS | stale pictures |
| `unresolved-replacement-sps-not-stale` | delayed | an IRAP picture whose newest SPS waits for its VPS, and the trailing pictures after it (closed GOP), are refused; the patched decode must not report reference errors from attempting them | stale pictures |
| `malformed-pending-sps` | delayed | a truncated pending SPS produces no pictures and is superseded by the later valid SPS | 0 pictures |
| `invalid-replacement-sps-keeps-state` | kept | a same-id SPS (invalid `chroma_format_idc`) that fails once its VPS arrives leaves the valid SPS/PPS usable | pass |
| `invalid-replacement-pps-keeps-state` | kept | same for a PPS (invalid default reference count) | pass |
| `corrupted-repeat-sps-mid-gop` | kept | a repeated SPS with a corrupted VPS id before a trailing picture does not interrupt decoding | pass |
| `corrupted-repeat-pps-mid-gop` | impact | a repeated PPS with a corrupted SPS id refuses pictures until the PPS is resent; the output must be a non-empty proper subsequence of the expected pictures, so neither a full stale decode nor no output passes | pass |
| `deferred-sps-uses-exact-length` | equivalent | an SPS ending in empty extensions and one payload bit short, whose length is not a whole number of bytes, is rejected when deferred exactly as on arrival (a byte-rounded late parse reads the stop bit as `sps_extension_4bits` and accepts it); the valid copy that follows decodes | — |
| `stale-sps-not-revived` | stale | a pending SPS superseded by a newer same-id SPS stays superseded when its VPS arrives | pass |
| `stale-pps-not-revived` | stale | same for a PPS | pass |
| `missing-dependency-never-arrives` | missing | slices whose PPS never resolves produce no pictures; later valid data decodes | pass |
| `flood-and-churn-bounded` | bounded | 20,000 PPS and 20,000 SPS whose dependencies never arrive plus 2,000 SPS replacements | pass |
| `vps-churn-large-dependants` | bounded | 16 SPS and 64 PPS of about 60 KiB each under 4,000 alternating VPS versions | pass |

For `bounded` fixtures, patched peak RSS must stay within unpatched + 64 MiB and
single-threaded decode time within twice unpatched + 1 s. The previous eager
revision (`9374c662`) took 4.35 s on `vps-churn-large-dependants` against 0.04 s
unpatched, which this limit rejects.

**Suite.** A vector passes only if the decoder exits successfully and its output
matches; `tests.py` checks this with a decoder that crashes after writing matching
bytes. With `--suite-reorder`, each vector is also decoded by the patched build with
every run of consecutive parameter sets reversed (runs containing the same id twice
are left alone); its output and exit status must equal the original order's,
including for vectors that fail identically in both orders. This
parses real conformance parameter sets, including VUI and HRD syntax, late.

**Mutation check** (manual, recorded below). Single-point breakages of the patch
were each rebuilt and run against the vector and fixtures.

## Recorded results

The raw runner report for the current patch is in [`evidence/`](evidence), under its
SHA-256 prefix; results apply only to the patch with that hash. Superseded revisions
are summarised below without their reports, which `run.py` reproduces. Host: an Apple M1
(linux-asahi 7.1.13, aarch64, GCC 16.1.1, x265 4.3, Python 3.14) used only as a
Linux build and software-decode host; base FFmpeg `bf1b838`.

### Current revision `a598cbf5…`

[`evidence/a598cbf5`](evidence/a598cbf5), 2026-09-18: `report.json` is the full
runner report (`run.py --sanitize` with the suite in `auto,single,frame4` and
`--suite-reorder`), built software-only; `mutations.json` the mutation results.

* **Vector:** unpatched exits 0 with the documented two pictures, `ec9f5857…`;
  patched gives six pictures at native sizes, `1ddf74263cb4953cfdfcf99c563d88ea`, in all
  three threading modes. The ASan/UBSan build matches with exit status 0 and no
  sanitizer report.
* **Fixtures:** 25/25 pass patched in all three modes (75 runs), and every fixture's
  unpatched expectation holds. 75/75 sanitized runs match with no report
  (LeakSanitizer enabled). `corrupted-repeat-pps-mid-gop` outputs 10 of the 17
  expected pictures, refusing 7, with no unexpected picture. Peak RSS /
  single-threaded time, unpatched vs patched: `flood-and-churn-bounded`
  538816 vs 538432 KiB, 0.33 vs 0.12 s; `vps-churn-large-dependants`
  69520 vs 80960 KiB, 0.03 vs 0.04 s (single runs).
* **JCT-VC-HEVC_V1 software suite**, identical in `auto`, `single` and `frame4`, pass
  requiring exit status 0 and matching output: unpatched 143/147, patched **144/147**.
  Newly passing: `VPSSPSPPS_A_MainConcept_1`. Regressions: none (exact per-vector
  pass sets compared). Failing in both builds: `SAODBLK_A_MainConcept_4`,
  `SAODBLK_B_MainConcept_4`, `TSUNEQBD_A_MAIN10_Technicolor_2`. These are FFmpeg
  software-decoder results, not the hardware 144/147 row.
* **Reordered suite:** all 143 vectors with a reversible parameter-set run decode
  identically to their original order (TSUNEQBD fails identically in both orders).
* **Mutations:** all 16 single-point breakages are caught, each by the fixture aimed
  at its rule. Three fixtures were strengthened during review because a mutation
  escaped them: the byte-rounded re-parse, the pictures after a refused IRAP, and
  the impact fixture, which now requires a non-empty proper subsequence so that a
  full stale decode cannot pass it (`unresolved-pps-not-refused` now fails it too).
* **Not covered by a fixture:** the `ps_refused_irap` reset in `hevc_decode_flush()`.
  The runner decodes files start to finish with the `ffmpeg` CLI and never seeks,
  so the flush path is verified by reading the code only.

### Superseded revision `8bf78183…`

`8bf78183…`: same behaviour as the current patch; it
carried a long policy comment on `HEVCPendingPS` (now in this README) and was
measured before the impact fixture required a proper subsequence.

### Superseded revision `10e5bc0f…`

`10e5bc0f…`: identical to `8bf78183` except that
`hevc_decode_flush()` did not reset `ps_refused_irap`, so a seek right after a refused
IRAP picture kept refusing pictures until the next IRAP. Its results match the current
ones (vector, 25/25 fixtures and 75 sanitized runs, 143/147 → 144/147, 143/143
reordered, 16/16 mutations).

### Superseded revision `9374c662…`

`9374c662…`: review found that it re-parsed pending
entries with byte-rounded length, re-parsed and copied every dependant when a VPS
or SPS changed (4.35 s vs 0.04 s on `vps-churn-large-dependants`), and refused
pictures after any corrupted repeated SPS. It passed the checks of that time: the
vector in all modes, 21/21 fixtures, 63 clean sanitized fixture runs,
JCT-VC-HEVC_V1 143/147 → 144/147 with no regressions, and 12/12 mutations.

### Superseded revision `7ed5ab15…`

`7ed5ab15…`: review found that it discarded pending
entries after a failed resolution, invalidated stored state on deferral, and that
the suite gate ignored exit status. Its results (vector in all modes, 14/14
fixtures of that time, 42 clean sanitized fixture runs, 143/147 → 144/147) do not
describe the current patch.

## Provenance and terms

* FFmpeg: `https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg.git` at
  `bf1b838f2ab88b4f8fd83443325c782ea0e0f7fa` (`n9.0.1`), LGPL-2.1-or-later. The patch
  is a derivative of those files under the same licence.
* Conformance vector and suite: ITU/JCT-VC bitstreams through Fluster
  `f3ad284a9e6cac70dc01b02e0de71c2994181d34`; terms not established, so
  download-on-demand for local testing only, per the driver repository's
  `docs/CORPUS.md` and `tests/corpus/manifest.json`. Nothing is committed.
* Synthetic fixtures: generated locally from FFmpeg lavfi test sources and
  libx265; streams and outputs are not committed.
* `source.json` pins the FFmpeg commit, patch SHA-256, vector identity (including
  the documented unpatched output) and suite definition; `tests.py` verifies the
  pins that do not need a download.

## Not done here

* No VA-API, V4L2 or Apple hardware decode, no `hwguard` lease, no client build
  installed or package pin changed. Exact client-build VA comparison and the full
  hardware HEVC suite remain in parent #15, which needs its own VA-enabled build.
* Known limits, from review: VideoToolbox builds its decoder configuration from
  the stored lists and does not see parameter sets that are still pending (before
  the patch they were dropped, so this is not a regression; VA-API is unaffected).
  A late parse copies the pending bytes again rather than reusing the shared
  buffer. `vps-churn-large-dependants` activates one picture at its end, so VPS
  versions alternating with IRAP pictures (about two parses per picture) are not
  measured, and the timing gate uses a single run with a 1 s margin. Later slices
  of a refused picture fail with "First slice in a frame missing" (traced in code;
  the single-slice fixtures do not reach it).
* FFmpeg's own FATE suite was not run (it needs the separate FATE sample set); the
  full JCT-VC-HEVC_V1 software comparison above is the regression gate used here.
* No upstream FFmpeg submission or report.
* Review: contributor self-checks and AI reviews (CodeRabbit CLI and Codex) of
  earlier revisions; no independent specialist parser-safety review has occurred.
  The corrupted-PPS trade-off and the resource bounds are the points that review
  should examine.
